children: The proceedings relate to alleged disclosure lapses involving related-party transactions and audit reports without valid peer review certificates

Five Adani Group companies have settled adjudication proceedings initiated by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) by collectively paying Rs 1.51 crore. The proceedings followed allegations concerning related-party transaction disclosures and compliance with audit-related requirements.
Under the settlement terms, Adani Enterprises paid Rs 76.05 lakh, while Adani Green Energy paid Rs 45.50 lakh. Adani Total Gas, AWL Agri Business and Adani Energy Solutions paid Rs 9.75 lakh each.
The settlement terms were recommended by Sebi’s High Powered Advisory Committee and subsequently accepted by the regulator’s panel of whole-time members.

The matter originated from Sebi’s examination of allegations raised in a 2023 report by short seller Hindenburg Research, which had flagged potential undisclosed related-party transactions and corporate governance concerns involving the Adani Group.

Sebi had issued show-cause notices to the five companies on 15 February 2024. One of the allegations concerned Adani Enterprises’ failure to disclose transactions between its subsidiary, Adani Estates, and Vakoder Investment in its FY13 annual report, as required under the applicable accounting standard and the erstwhile listing agreement.
The notices also raised concerns over audit and limited review reports issued for several group companies during different quarters between 2015 and 2021.
According to the allegations, the reports had been signed by chartered accountancy firms Dharmesh Parikh & Co LLP and Shah Dhandharia & Co LLP without valid peer review certificates.
The regulator’s order stated that the adjudication proceedings were being disposed of after Sebi accepted the settlement terms and received the settlement amount from the applicants.

The proceedings were closed under Section 15JB of the Sebi Act and Section 23JA of the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act, read with Regulation 23(1) of the Settlement Regulations. The order disposed of the proceedings on the basis of the accepted settlement terms.
